evidence: The sparse estimate stores both nonzero values and index metadata.
why_it_matters: Sparse memory savings are lower than the raw zero-weight percentage suggests.

finding: Low sparsity can use more memory than dense storage.
evidence: With value_bytes=4 and index_bytes=4, sparse storage at 25% sparsity is larger than dense fp32 storage.
why_it_matters: Sparsity is not automatically a memory win unless sparsity is high enough or the sparse format is efficient.

finding: Around 50% sparsity is the break-even point in this simple unstructured model.
evidence: At 50% sparsity, nonzero values plus indices roughly equal dense fp32 memory.
why_it_matters: Below this level, sparse storage overhead can cancel the benefit of zero weights.

finding: High sparsity can reduce parameter memory significantly.
evidence: At 75% and 90% sparsity, sparse parameter memory becomes lower than dense parameter memory.
why_it_matters: Sparsity can be useful for memory reduction when sparsity is high and sparse storage is supported.

finding: This is analytical storage estimation, not real sparse runtime profiling.
evidence: The simulation does not run sparse CUDA kernels or measure latency.
why_it_matters: Sparse runtime benefits depend on hardware, kernels, sparse format, and workload shape.
